title: E2E: wildmat group filter end-to-end acceptance test
description:
## What
End-to-end test that reads a TOML config with wildmat patterns, starts the transit pipeline, ingests test articles, and asserts the correct groups were accepted and rejected — verifying the full acceptance criteria from the epic.

## Algorithm
Test in crates/integration-tests/ or crates/transit/tests/:

1. Build transit Config from TOML:
   [groups]
   names = ["comp.*", "sci.*", "!alt.binaries.*", "alt.test"]
2. Call Config::validate(); assert Ok
3. Build GroupFilter from config; build ValidationConfig with that filter
4. For each test article below, call validate_article_ingress() then run_pipeline():
   - Article A: Newsgroups: comp.lang.rust → expect accepted, log entry for comp.lang.rust
   - Article B: Newsgroups: sci.math → expect accepted, log entry for sci.math
   - Article C: Newsgroups: alt.binaries.pictures → expect filtered (no log entry)
   - Article D: Newsgroups: alt.test → expect accepted (exact match after negation miss)
   - Article E: Newsgroups: rec.humor → expect filtered (no match in pattern list)
5. Assert log entry counts match expectations
6. Assert validate_article_ingress rejects Article C and E before pipeline (ValidationConfig filter)

## Defensive programming rules
- Use in-memory SQLite for all state
- Test articles have deterministic Message-IDs (no random UUIDs)
- Each article has From:, Date:, Subject: headers to pass mandatory header check
- No network calls; use mock IPFS block store or LMDB in-process

## Agent team
Standard: Agent R (read integration test setup pattern in crates/integration-tests/), Agent I (write E2E test), Agent V (cargo test -p stoa-integration-tests + full workspace)

## Tests
The test IS the deliverable. 5 articles × 2 assertions = 10 assertions total.
Oracle: epic acceptance criteria (hardcoded expected results).
